signal: [STRUCTURAL FINDING — WHY THERE ARE ALMOST NO ATM TENDERS] A sweep of the UJN notices database (761,626 notices) and the contract register (1,674,409 contracts, both re-counted 27/08/2026) returns essentially NO ATM procurement: the title term 'банкомат' returns ZERO notices and 'bankomat' zero, and the contract register returns exactly ONE contract mentioning ATMs in the entire register — 'Услуге померања банкомата' (ATM RELOCATION services), 13/06/2024, buyer Sportski centar 'Tašmajdan' d.o.o., winner Miodrag Brkić PR / M.B. Tim Beograd (PIB 103692783), RSD 11,707.69, CPV 98300000 — i.e. a haulage job, not ATM supply or servicing. CPV 32442000 (terminal equipment) returns 6 contracts in the whole register, of which exactly ONE falls in 2026: NBS 'набавка ПОС терминала', 30/04/2026, RSD 150,000, WINNER Payten d.o.o. (PIB 110428879), contract Г.бр. 3385. The register also shows a MUCH larger NBS terminal contract the earlier sweep missed: 'Мобилни терминали' (mobile terminals), 25/11/2025, RSD 4,080,000, WINNER Info-Kod Rešenja d.o.o. (PIB 106780962), contract no. 17032 — 27x the Payten value. The absence is structural: Serbia's commercial banks are private and outside the Public Procurement Act, and Banka Poštanska štedionica — the state-owned bank that DOES run ATMs — states on its own site that it 'није обвезник Закона о јавним набавкама' (is not subject to the Public Procurement Act) and publishes only on posted.co.rs. The National Bank of Serbia, the only bank-type buyer on the portal, does not operate a public ATM estate. Serbian ATM demand is therefore invisible to the portal by design and must be tracked bank-by-bank.
source_name: Portal javnih nabavki (UJN) notice + contract-register sweep (re-run 27/08/2026) + posted.co.rs procurement policy statement
implies: Do not read 'no ATM tenders in Serbia' as no demand — the whole Serbian ATM/self-service market is bought privately. The only two published routes are posted.co.rs (Banka Poštanska štedionica, check every run) and vendor/press announcements; everything else needs direct bank coverage — Raiffeisen Serbia (existing Printec x-core reference), AikBank (existing NCR recycler reference), Banca Intesa (Diebold Nixdorf/Payten incumbent), NLB Komercijalna, OTP Srbija, UniCredit, Addiko. The corollary for terminals: the portal DOES surface NBS terminal buying, and it shows Payten is not the only supplier inside NBS — Info-Kod Rešenja took a RSD 4.08m mobile-terminal contract there in Nov-2025.
likelihood: Permanent structural feature of the Serbian market
followup: Keep posted.co.rs on the every-run checklist, and hand Serbian commercial-bank ATM coverage to the company/competitor agents rather than to procurement-portal monitoring. Add Info-Kod Rešenja d.o.o. (PIB 106780962) to the Serbian terminal-competitor list alongside Payten, and correct any brief that says Payten is the sole terminal supplier at NBS.
